title: Apple iOS 7 website, 2013
lede: Apple’s launch page for iOS 7: very thin type on white and the new flat icons, under the old glossy navigation bar.
summary: Ultra-thin “iOS 7” headline and a phone showing the flatter iOS 7 icons; the navigation bar is still glossy. September 2013.

evidence.note: Captured with `tools/capture.mjs` (headless Chrome, 1440 × 900) on 28 September 2026 from the Wayback Machine copy of 20 September 2013, and inspected. The screenshot shows the first viewport; the measurement covers up to four screens. Nothing covers the page. The headlines are images, so their weight is not measured.

styles.note: Borderline: the thin type and flatter icons show the iOS 7 turn to flat design, but the page has few color fills, the navigation bar is glossy, and the icons keep soft gradients.

observed: A gray navigation bar with a top highlight, vertical dividers, and a rounded search field runs across the top.
Under a thin gray rule, “iOS 7” and the line “The mobile OS from a whole new perspective.” are set in very thin, large dark gray type, centered on white.
A white iPhone lies at an angle below. Its screen shows the iOS 7 home screen: rounded-square icons in bright colors, with simple glyphs and soft gradients, on a dark blue starry wallpaper.
interpretation: Measured: 7% of screenshot pixels are saturated, and 65% of boxes have a 1 px border, so the capture fails the color and border ranges. The glossy navigation bar is an image the extractor cannot see.

The page shows the flat turn in type and icons before Apple removed the gloss from its site navigation; NN/g dates Apple’s fully flat navigation to 2015 ([NN/g](ref:nngroup-flat-design-article-2015)).
borrow: Use a very thin weight at a very large size for a single headline on white, and let the colored content carry the color.

images.alt: Apple iOS 7 page of September 2013: a glossy gray navigation bar, the headline iOS 7 and a subtitle in very thin dark gray type on white, and a white iPhone at an angle showing colorful iOS 7 app icons.
images.caption: First viewport of the [Wayback Machine copy of apple.com, 20 September 2013](https://web.archive.org/web/20130920043843/http://www.apple.com/ios/).
